extracted.subtask_description: Official annual report summarizing U.S. immigration enforcement, statistics, administrative duties, and suggested legislation for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1911. Contains statutory duties, classification rules, required statistical tables, causes for exclusion/deportation, and administrative procedures (appeals, bonds, reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of information duties (section 40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 40 the Commissioner General is authorized to establish a 'division of information' whose duty is 'to promote a beneficial distribution of aliens admitted into the United States among the several States and Territories desiring immigration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The division shall gather from all available sources useful information regarding the resources, products, and physical characteristics of each State and Territory, publish such information in different languages and distribute the publications among all admitted aliens who may ask for such information at immigrant stations and to such other persons as may desire the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficial distribution—definition and intent
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Beneficial distribution' means a distribution that will benefit both the alien and the locality to which he goes; another purpose, incidental rather than immediate, being the benefiting of congested localities (cities) by inducing aliens not to go there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution should aim to benefit both immigrant and locality, including preventing further concentration in already overcrowded urban centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: State/Territory agents' access to admitted aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: When any State or Territory appoints and maintains an agent or agents to represent it at immigrant stations, such agents shall, under regulations prescribed by the Commissioner-General of Immigration and subject to the approval of the Secretary of Commerce and Labor, have access to aliens who have been admitted to the United States for the purpose of presenting, either orally or in writing, the special inducements offered by such State or Territory to aliens to settle thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access by State/Territorial agents is permitted but must conform to Commissioner-General regulations and Secretary approval; communication may be oral or written and should present settlement inducements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical limitations on distribution schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Various practical difficulties that must be considered in any scheme for distributing immigrants rather than allowing them to concentrate in established localities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlined difficulties include: (1) it may be too late to stem the existing tide toward certain localities with established immigrant nuclei; (2) distributed aliens will not remain unless placement matches their desires and they are physically/mentally adapted; (3) distribution is not a cure-all for immigration-related evils; (4) distribution schemes may inadvertently increase immigration and benefit intermediaries (steamship lines, labor agencies) rather than solve problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical classification rule for immigrant/emigrant and nonimmigrant/nonemigrant
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions used in compiling statistics: (1) immigrant and emigrant relate to permanent arrivals and departures; (2) nonimmigrant and nonemigrant relate to temporary arrivals and departures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arriving aliens whose permanent domicile has been outside the United States who intend to reside permanently in the United States are classed as immigrant aliens; departing aliens whose permanent residence has been in the U.S. who intend to reside permanently abroad are classed as emigrant aliens. Temporary trips are classed as nonemigrant (outward) and nonimmigrant (inward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statistical tables and core data elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The report prescribes/uses a series of tables (I to XXII etc.) and specific variables to summarize the year's work and provide detailed analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core elements include: arrivals and departures by immigrant/nonimmigrant and emigrant/nonemigrant classes; number rejected and expelled after entry; arrivals/departures of citizens; net increases by months, countries, races; occupations (professional, skilled, miscellaneous); sex, age, literacy, financial condition, how passage was paid, whether coming to join a relative or friend; length of prior residence for emigrants; head tax collected; stowaways; alien seamen deserters; arrests and deportations broken out by cause and statutory category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation categorization in statistics (professional/skilled/unskilled)
rubrics_metrics.description: Occupations of aliens entering and leaving are segregated into professional, skilled, and miscellaneous (commonly used as 'unskilled').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report compares numbers in these occupational classes for arrivals and departures and discusses economic implications (e.g., inflow of unskilled labor vs. skilled trades).

rubrics_metrics.name: Illiteracy and age-group reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report records ages (e.g., under 14, 14–44, 45 and over) and literacy status (can read/write, read but not write, neither read nor write) for arrivals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illiteracy rates are reported as percentages of admitted aliens over 14 and compared year-to-year to indicate education trends among migrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial condition and proof at inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of money shown to inspection officers by arriving aliens is tabulated, including counts by categories (under $50, $50 or over).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess immigrants' means on arrival and the proportion assisted by relatives or friends; the report notes limitations of ocular demonstration and reliability of such self-reported data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Idiots
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens classed as 'Idiots' are excludable and counted among rejections at ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table XVII (and comparisons across years) shows numbers rejected for this cause; used as a statutory exclusion category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Imbeciles
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens classed as 'Imbeciles' are excludable and recorded in rejection statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in multi-year comparative rejections tables as a distinct excludable class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Feeble-minded persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens classed as 'Feeble-minded persons' are excludable and tabulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among mental/psychological exclusion categories in the causes-of-rejection comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Insanity (including epileptics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens afflicted with insanity, including epileptics, are excludable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counted annually in the rejections table; grouped with other mental-health exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Likely to become a public charge (including paupers and beggars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens likely to become a public charge are excludable; the category explicitly includes paupers and beggars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This economic/public-support exclusion is tracked year-to-year and is a major ground for refusal; the report discusses public-charge determinations and their consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Afflicted with contagious disease
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens afflicted with contagious disease are excludable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contagious-disease exclusions are reported in rejection tallies and influence public-health enforcement at ports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Afflicted with tuberculosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens afflicted with tuberculosis are excludable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tuberculosis treated as a distinct ground for exclusion and counted separately in tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Physically or mentally defective
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens who are physically or mentally defective are excludable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broader category captures assorted physical/mental conditions leading to exclusion and is included in comparative tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens who are criminals are excludable and recorded as a cause for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal exclusion counts are maintained and compared across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Prostitutes and other immoral women
rubrics_metrics.description: Prostitutes and other immoral women are excludable classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically significant exclusion category; the report includes counts and notes related deportation provisions (including changes under the white-slave act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Procurers of prostitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurers (pimps) are an excludable class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated separately in the causes-of-rejection statistics and in deportation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of rejection: Contract laborers
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract laborers are an excludable class under the immigration laws and are tabulated as a cause for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among exclusion causes and compared across years in Table XVII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrests and deportations classifications (Table XVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrests and deportations are segregated into general classes: 'Deportation compulsory within 3 years,' 'Deportation compulsory without time limit,' and 'Public charges within 1 year after entry, from subsequent causes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under each general heading the report shows specific causes for deportation; notes legislative change (white-slave act of March 26, 1910) abolished the three-year limitation for sexually immoral classes, enabling deportation without time limit for that class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deportation specifics and counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of deported aliens are broken down by reason: excluded at entry but deported within 3 years, became public charges from causes existing prior to entry, became prostitutes after entry, entered without inspection, immoral women deported without time limit, procurers, aliens supported by proceeds of prostitution, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report gives totals and subcategory counts (e.g., of 2,708 aliens under the first heading: 1,151 were excluded classes at time of entry, 857 became public charges from prior causes, 129 became prostitutes after entry, 555 entered without inspection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and admission under bond (Section 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: 'the decision of any two members of a board [of special inquiry] shall prevail, but either the alien or any dissenting member of the said board may appeal through the commissioner of immigration at the port of arrival and the Commissioner General of Immigration to the Secretary of Commerce and Labor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report provides appeal statistics (e.g., 8,433 appeals passed upon, with 2,858 aliens admitted outright, 1,368 on bond, 4,075 affirmed rejections, etc.) and also covers direct applications for admission under bond (210 applications, 154 granted, 56 denied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Head tax collection and financial reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables report number of taxable aliens and head tax collected; financial statement compares appropriation and expenditures for conducting the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 913,880 aliens taxable; $3,655,513 collected in the year; appropriation $2,575,000 with $2,277,311.78 spent — report notes immigration act became a revenue producer and shows the balance between amount collected and appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alien seamen desertion reporting and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Masters of vessels are required to report alien seamen desertions (Table XX); enforcement complicated by inaccurate reporting and by court decisions (Taylor case) affecting head tax enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report notes difficulty obtaining accurate information from steamship lines, legal impediments (Supreme Court decision 207 U.S. 120), and gives enforcement examples including fines and imprisonments arising from investigations (e.g., Hellenic Transatlantic Steam Navigation Co. case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stowaways reporting and legislative remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Table XXI reports stowaways brought to U.S. ports (e.g., 528 in the past year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report references H.R. 32441 as proposed legislation which, if enacted or merged with the Bureau's proposed measure, would help abate stowaway and related evils; suggests legislative remedies are part of administrative response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net population change adjustments (naturalized citizens abroad)
rubrics_metrics.description: To compute absolutely correct net increase from immigration, the number of naturalized citizens of the United States who have left the country for permanent residence abroad should be deducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report notes inability to obtain figures on naturalized citizens leaving, so reported net increase (e.g., 512,085) may not be absolutely precise without this deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative multi-year tables for trend analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The report uses multi-year comparative tables (e.g., Table XVII a) to track causes of rejection across years and identify trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons from previous years inform policy and enforcement discussion; separate tables (e.g., Table XVII b) deal with special rejection phases such as residents of contiguous foreign territories refused temporary entry.
